posts.text:
🇮🇱🇺🇸🇮🇷 Israel is spending $750 million on global PR. They bought access to 25 million U.S. conservative profiles. They're testing messages on them right now.

Murtaza Hussain, national security reporter at Drop Site News, joins Brandon to explain the influence operation and why it isn’t working.

Israel has lost the Democratic base completely. All they have left is the right. So they commissioned a study that found the most effective approach: don’t talk about Israel. Make conservatives hate Muslims instead. Then hope the support follows.

The platform they’re using is Parler. A company briefly owned it, sold it, then kept selling access to its user base. That company contracted with the Israeli government to data-test pro-Israel messaging on 25 million conservatives, optimize what lands, and push it out at scale.

But Hussain says it isn’t working. Every trend is moving in the opposite direction. Gen Z on the right is vocally anti-Israel. Even older MAGA voters who don’t follow the politics closely are feeling the economic pain of a war they were promised would never happen.

Trump campaigned explicitly against war with Iran. Then Netanyahu lobbied him into one. That is a betrayal that no influence operation can paper over.

On escalation: Hussain says the carrier group moving to the region is the signal to watch, not what anyone is saying publicly. Assets don’t lie. He puts end-of-November as the most logical window if Trump moves. 

But the political conditions are in flux, the Senate has changed hands, and the December 11th funding deadline could complicate any escalation.

Meanwhile, every round of strikes pushes more of Iran's missile production underground. The last air war failed to destroy their capacity. The next one won’t, either.

@MazMHussain @WeTheBrandon

posts.text:
🇮🇷🇮🇱🇺🇦 The blockade is strangling Iran. At some point, Iran strikes back. That point is coming soon.

Dimitri Lascaris, lawyer, journalist, and activist who reported from inside the Strait of Hormuz at the height of the war, joins Brandon to explain why escalation is inevitable and why Tehran may fire the first shot.

There are only 3 ways this plays out: peace, status quo, or escalation. Lascaris rules out the first two.

Trump says Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon. Iran has 60% enriched uranium and the capacity to enrich further. There's no deal that closes that gap.

The blockade is doing severe economic damage. Iran’s supreme leader has already ordered an end to the state of no peace, no war. If the U.S. holds back, Lascaris says Tehran escalates anyway.

On Israel: Lascaris doesn’t buy the idea that Israel controls U.S. foreign policy. When something truly matters to Washington, Israel does what it's told. Any talk of going it alone on Iran is chest-pounding. If it happens, the U.S. is 100% behind it.

On Ukraine: Russia is winning on territory, casualties, and infrastructure. But if drone and missile attacks on Russian soil continue, Lascaris sees no path that doesn’t eventually force Russia to strike NATO.

The people are the only brakes on any of it...

@dimitrilascaris
